text: Would you tell us just exactly what happened Tuesday at noon when the saucer landed?
Well, I'll tell you the story from the beginning.
It was about 11 o'clock Tuesday morning, and I was looking out my window, and I heard this
terrible, slurring noise like a mobby diner on a flip table.
Uh-huh.
And, uh, with the jet school here for much, I didn't make any sense to it.
And all of a sudden, that huge thing settled down on my yard,
and at first I didn't know if the roof came off of my house or what it was, you know.
Wasn't there much vibration?
Nothing at all.
No reason whatsoever.
It just settled down.
Did you see this thing landing?
I did.
And how did it come in, like a book?
It came straight down.
straight down at a high rate of speed?
No, no, no. It was real slow, just like an elevator.
Uh-huh.
Real steady and slow. I don't think it sat quite on the ground. It just hovered there.
Like a helicopter?
Yeah, but it didn't leave any marks on the ground, and that's why I don't think it settled here
I was just wondering if it was a short time that I couldn't see everything.
Oh, were you alone when you saw this?
Oh, yes. Yes.
And what did you do when it hovered over the ground? Did you run out there?
I ran outside right quick, just like I would if a car would drive up.
And a hatch opened in the top of the machine, and a man standing there, and he held up a thing that looked like a water jug, which it turned out to be.
He didn't say anything. He didn't say a word. All he moistened, he wanted water. You know, like you moistened you want a drink.
Uh-huh.
So I took the jug and I filled it for him and I brought it back.
And while I'm filling the jug, I was thinking, what could I do?
I didn't come up with any answers.
So I handed him up the jug, which was about almost six feet up to his neck.
They were in the top part of the machine and I presume the bottom part of it was all mortar or something.
Me? Well you saw the one man.
There were three of them.
All three of them got out?
No, none of them got out. None of them got out. They stayed right in the place.
Well did this thing have windows in it?
Nope.
Well how could you tell there were more than one?
Because I could see in there through the open hatch.
Well, this sensor was on the top. It was on the top half of this machine, see?
Uh-huh.
And you could see in there like there was indirect lighting or something. I don't know. It was immaculate inside. I'm getting ahead of my story.
Yes.
When I handed him the water, one man was cooking these little pancake things.
And I don't know why I did it, but I motioned.
I pointed to him, and I made a motion with my mouth like eating.
One man that took the water, he looked down at me, and he reached over,
and he got four of these little cakes in the hands of thousands.
And he closed the hat.
That was it.
Then he took off.
What do these men look like?
Well, they look like Italians.
What they look like, they were about five foot tall, 120 pounds, I presume.
And they were wearing a black jersey-looking clothes.
You know what I mean?
They had two-piece-off-fit turtleneck snow buttons.
And they had a form-fitting cap on like they wore a helmet over at some time.
Now these other two men didn't even look at me. One was at the instrument board.
I presume holding a chip there. He didn't even turn around. He stayed right there.
One cooking these things. He stayed at his boat.
Well, they look like normal human beings.
Normal human beings. Their eyes were just like ours and they had to arm everything.
Except the height.
The height was white, only, you know, it was dark and bright, bright material.
What else did you see inside of it?
I could see three of these, the instrument board.
There were about, oh, I would say three foot by four foot.
And each one of them had an iron, like an iron fan around them, you know, about three
foot high, like a protection.
And on each side of those iron fans there was a stabilizing cable or rope or something
with a, you know, a snap in it.
These men standing there, they had rings on the side of their clothes or else a pelt.
I couldn't detect just what it was. They were tapping in when they got in the station, see?
Well, Mr. Simonton, when this one fellow motioned for water and you brought it out to him, were you frightened?
No, no, I wasn't scared. I didn't see him.
He doesn't have to be scared of it. He had no firearms and no weapons or nothing on him.
He's normal, so I gave it to him.
I was friendly with him. He was friendly with me, so that was it.
Well, now, what about these pancakes?
Did they give you three of those?
They gave me four of them.
Four of them?
Yeah. I sent one in. Our county judge, Carter, sent one in to work and burn out.
Did you notify Judge Carter about this?
Oh, that was about two people yesterday, I guess.
Well, you saw this saucer on Tuesday around noon.
But nobody was raising.
But did you talk to other people before?
I talked to other people before I talked to Judge Carter, yes.
And what did they say? What was their reaction?
They thought it was a big joke.
A big joke? What does Judge Carter think?
Oh, he, uh, he belongs to the, uh, flying saucer club, but he just sank it with the joke.
He hit the man that looked almost like Chris Smith.
Uh-huh.
He's under the believer story.
Oh, yeah.
Yeah, everybody's believing it now because I've got the evidence.
Well, now, you see, they sent one in to Washington for analysis.
When did they send it?
Uh, I don't know where he's at.
We'd have to contact him.
Well, what happened to the other three?
I got them.
Have you eaten any of them?
I tasted a bite of what?
What do they like?
They taste just like a piece of cardboard.
It has no more flavor to it than nothing.
Now, what's the...
The texture of them, they're very thin, and they're porous.
You hold it up to the light and they look like a...
a grapefruit vint, if you know what that is.
Uh-huh.
They rig up this and they saw it. There's no, uh, there's no fakie sign of it.
It doesn't make a raise in there.
How much is that engine?
What is it, a four-inch?
When you, uh, put it on the stool, it looks like a synthetic rubber or something.
I don't know what it is.
They resemble a flathead, you say?
Yeah, that's what you resemble. They're about two inches wide and about three inches long.
Like, you know, boy, that one's better on than the other one.
Uh-huh.
And everything in this plane was black, like, uh, not iron, you know what I mean?
It was dull black, and it just looked immaculate in there, what I could see.
Now this machine was 30 feet wide. I stepped off the imaginary line and it could be 28, it could be 32, but it was about 30 feet wide, about 12 feet high in the center.
It was a huge machine.
Then I saw that he gave me these sandpipes.
He closed the hat.
I heard a latch, and you couldn't see on the outside where that hat was.
It fit so tight.
You couldn't even see a feet or nothing there.
Then he started to raise.
Raised up, oh, maybe 20 feet high, something like that.
It's like an elevator.
And all the while they were sitting here, there was a motor like running.
There was a humming noise in there, like a big heavy electric motor running.
So I presume that the guy at the control board was holding that machine there.
And then it raised up slowly like that, then all of a sudden it just went straight south
on a 45 degree up and a two-circuit that was clear out of sight.
How long would you say we were there altogether?
About over five minutes.
Now, are there any marks on the...
No marks, no marks whatsoever.
The only evidence that the Army or anybody could get would be on top of a pine tree here
where they took off and hit that so high it almost bent over.
And that's about the only thing there is.
But there are markings on the ground.
That's the funny thing.
Mr. Simonson, am I correct in assuming you did get into this hatch or you didn't?
No, no, no, no.
But you could see in there?
I could see in there from where I was standing.
The hatch raised up like the trunk of a car, you know?
Uh-huh.
Raised up and then raised foot, just like that.
But this hatch was above the level of 10 or 12 feet off the ground, wasn't it?
Well, it was about 6 feet where it opened.
See, the center of the machine.
The center of the machine, there was just like two great big poles put together.
You know what I mean?
The top and the bottom looked just like no wheels, no nothing.
But you could see onto the inside of it.
I could see the inside part of it.
I could see that much.
I could see the cooking things.
I could see three of these instrument boards.
What else was in there I couldn't see.
Uh, something like that, but I couldn't see in the whole face, just from that small net.
The boat was about 30 inches wide and about 6 foot long, you know, when it raised up.
And I had to reach up quite high to have this water, and the net never got out.
None of them got out.
And I had my left hand on the machine, not thinking about radioactivity, but nothing happened to me yet.
Well, Mr. Simonson, what does your family think about this?
Well, my family isn't here. My wife is working in Chicago. If she isn't here, I'm all alone.
But nobody else was there at the time.
That's right. Nobody would go by. I lived right out of the back of my house, and nobody went by us that time.
So the only proof I got is these faticates.
Uh-huh.
And my workforce.
When did the authorities say they expected an analysis back from Washington?
They said it won't take a week anyhow to get it.
A week?
Yeah.
And the, well, all the papers have been calling me, and I ain't long bit.
So they got us through the Philadelphia Press, as you saw it there.
Mm-hmm.
Sentinel and the Journal and one radio station in Minneapolis called me.
Uh-huh.
So how many people now that you talk to before you got a hold of Jesse Carter?
Oh, gosh, I don't know.
Just when I go up to town, people in my own neighborhood, in Eagle River, they ask me about it.
I just go around talking to them, they ask me.
And their general reaction was that it was a joke.
That's right.
And the few of them that have read up on this, they believe it.
And now everybody believes it.
Everybody up there believes it.
I don't care if nobody believes it. I know it's right.
If they don't want to believe it, that's up to them.
I know what I saw and that's it.
Well, Mr. Simonson, why do you think of this whole thing?
Well, really, I don't know what to think of it.
I know it's taken up a lot of my time, and I'm not thinking anything.
All I'm looking at, I'm a bummer, see?
Mm-hmm.
And, uh, right now, it's my busy season.
Of course, anybody wants any information, I'm glad to give some.
But, uh, you see, it's getting so that cars coming in, it's bothering me and everything.
Would you tend to think that this thing is from outer space?
Would that be your guess?
I said, what?
Yes.
Why didn't they stop some here?
I said, what?
Why didn't they save some?
Did you ask them to let him go?
I didn't stay away from them.
I was going through, and they closed the hatch, and I flicked, you know, and got out of there.
That's it.
So in other words, all you think this fellow was after was water.
That was after water.
That's right.
In exchange for a few pancakes.
Well, I was friendly with him, and I moistened my partner to the pancakes.
I didn't think he'd give me any.
Or you're eating, you know.
He's up at sea and he's up there with them and he's over at the port of Anthepon.
But now, say these stories didn't come up in the sun,
is there anything that would make you believe they were different than an ordinary human being on Earth?
The only thing is they were, they were small.
They were about five foot tall.
They were well built for boys.
Oh.
Oh, about the same age, oh, I would say under 20, 20, 25 to 30, somewhere around there.

And they were really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really,
I've seen a lot of bright things on cars and that, but this thing, I'll tell you, I can't
explain how bright it was.
Out of the water, Jeff, that they gave me, it was a, oh, it was a density.
It was made out of what they looked like the same material.
It was bright inside and out.
And it wasn't, it wasn't light as aluminum, and yet it didn't seem as heavy as steel.
Well, it wasn't too heavy.
But it was made on a service pattern, you know what I mean?
Uh-huh.
And, uh, while I was filling it, I was looking at it.
It had a handle on each side of the top, like a big box, you know?
Yes.
And, uh, the part of it was metal also, and it just squished in.
It just threw it.
It was passed through the jug by a flexible cable wire or something.
It wasn't keyed, you know.
You know, so it wouldn't lose weight or anything.
Uh-huh.
And I put the card here.
I gave him the water.
And he gave me the panic case.
And he closed the hatch just right now like that.
That was it.
That was your indication that they wanted to take off.
Oh, yes, they did.
Oh, I was standing there, but I was old, maybe 20, 25 feet from it.
I couldn't feel any trash, any breeze, nothing.
I just, uh...
So what would you guess, what kind of propulsion pushed him off?
I have no sign of that.
That's a...
...raising up the bridge.
It looked like some kind of gravity on the boat.
But when they took off, it was the normal, the flat.
